questions.questionText: Three towns P, Q and R are such that the distance between Q and R is double that between P and Q. A car covers the distance between P and Q with a speed 36 km/h and the distance between Q and R with a speed 48 km/h. The average speed for the entire journey is:

solutions.newText:
"THIS IS A HIGH WEIGHTAGE TOPIC"


If t1 is time taken during 1st part of the journey, t2 is time taken for 2nd part of the journey and t is total time (t1 + t2) of the journey then assuming d to be the distance between P and Q, 
$${t_1} = \frac{d}{{{v_1}}},{t_2} = \frac{2d}{{{v_2}}},t = \frac{{\left( {{2v_1} + {v_2}} \right)d}}{{{v_1}{v_2}}}$$

Since average speed = Total distance/total time taken,

Average speed $$=\frac{{3d}}{t} = \frac{{3{v_1}{v_2}}}{{{2v_1} + {v_2}}}$$

Average speed of a body \[ = \frac{{3{v_1}{v_2}}}{{{2v_1} + {v_2}}} = \frac{{3 \times 36 \times 48}}{{120}}\] = 43.2 km/h

questions.questionText: A particle is moving in a straight line and passes through a point $O$ with a velocity of $6\;m{s^{ - 1}}.$The particle moves with a constant retardation of $2\;m{s^{ - 2}}\;$for 4 s and there after moves with constant velocity. How long after leaving $O$ does the particle return to $O$?
topics: Kinematic Equations for Uniformly Accelerated Motion
mainTags: Equations of uniformly accelerated motion in one dimension

solutions.newText:
"THIS IS A HIGH WEIGHTAGE TOPIC"

Let the particle moves toward right with velocity 6 m/s. Due to retardation after time ${t_1}$its velocity becomes zero.

From $v = u - a\,t$⇒ $0 = 6 - 2 \times {t_1}$ ⇒ ${t_1} = 3\,\sec $
But retardation works on it for 4 sec. It means after reaching point A direction of motion get reversed and acceleration works on the particle for next one second.
${S_{OA}} = u\,{t_1} - \frac{1}{2}a\,t_1^2$$ = 6 \times 3 - \frac{1}{2}(2)\;{(3)^2} = 18 - 9 = 9m$
${S_{AB}} = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times {(1)^2} = 1m$
$\therefore $ ${S_{BC}} = {S_{OA}} - {S_{AB}}$ $ = 9 - 1$$ = 8m$
Now velocity of the particle at point B in return journey
$v = 0 + 2 \times 1$$ = 2m/s$    (using v = u + at)
In return journey from B to C, particle moves with constant velocity 2 m/s to cover the distance 8m.
Time taken $ = \frac{{{\text{Distance }}}}{{{\text{Velocity}}}} = \frac{8}{2} = 4\sec $
Total time taken by particle to return at point O is ⇒$T = {t_{OA}} + {t_{AB}} + {t_{BC}}$$ = 3 + 1 + 4 = 8\sec $

analysisTags: Kinematic Equations for Uniformly Accelerated Motion

questions.questionText: Two bodies begin a free fall from the same height at a time interval of $${\text{N}}\,{\text{s}}$$. If vertical separation between the two bodies is $${\text{1 m}}$$ after $$n$$ second from the start of the first body, then $$n$$ is equal to $(n > N)$

Let $${y_1}$$ be the height through which  body 1 falls in n seconds and $${y_2}$$ be the height through which body 2 falls in (n - N) seconds (because body 2 starts after N seconds) then since there starting velocity $$u = 0$$, we can write

$${y_1} = \frac{1}{2}g{n^2},{y_2} = \frac{1}{2}g{\left( {n - N} \right)^2}$$

$$\therefore {y_1} - {y_2} = \frac{1}{2}g\left[ {{n^2} - {{\left( {n - N} \right)}^2}} \right]$$

$$ \Rightarrow 1 = \frac{g}{2}\left( {2n - N} \right)N$$             $$\left[ {\because {y_1} - {y_2} = 1} \right]$$

$$ \Rightarrow n = \frac{1}{{gN}} + \frac{N}{2}$$

$\alpha ,\,\beta ,\,\,\gamma \,\,$ are the roots of equation $8{x^3} + 1001x + 2008 = 0$
Sum of roots $ = - \left( {\frac{{coeff.\,\,of\,\,{x^2}}}{{coeff.\,\,of\,\,{x^3}}}} \right)$

$\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 0\,\,$ then
$\alpha + \beta = - \gamma $
$\beta + \gamma = - \alpha $
$\gamma + \alpha = - \beta $
Now,
${\left( {\alpha + \beta } \right)^3} + {\left( {\beta + \gamma } \right)^3} + {\left( {\gamma + \alpha } \right)^{^3}}$
${\left( {\alpha + \beta } \right)^3} + {\left( {\beta + \gamma } \right)^3} + {\left( {\gamma + \alpha } \right)^{^3}} = {\left( { - \gamma } \right)^3} + {\left( { - \alpha } \right)^3} + {\left( { - \beta } \right)^3}$

We know,
${a^3} + {b^3} + {c^3} - 3abc = \left( {a + b + c} \right)\left( {{a^2} + {b^2} + {c^2} - ab - bc - ca} \right)$
$ \Rightarrow {\left( {\alpha + \beta } \right)^3} + {\left( {\beta + \gamma } \right)^3} + {\left( {\gamma + \alpha } \right)^3}$
$ = - \left[ {3\alpha \beta \gamma + \left( {\alpha + \beta + \gamma } \right)\left( {{\alpha ^2} + {\beta ^2} + {\gamma ^2} - \alpha \beta - \beta \gamma - \gamma \alpha } \right)} \right]$
